reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E4) does not provide specific support for the key premises. E1 discusses synthesis and aggregation of HEA nanoparticles but not size-dependent melting depression or surface premelting. E2 describes thermal analysis of a different HEA powder but does not address nanoparticle size effects. E4 reports a disorder-to-order phase transition in ultrasmall nanoparticles but does not study melting behavior or surface premelting. The premises rely on general surface-energy concepts not substantiated by the cited passages.
premises: Sub-10 nm nanoparticles exhibit a size-dependent depression of melting temperature by ~200°C relative to larger particles
Surface atoms in small nanoparticles have diminished cohesive energy, leading to a liquid-like surface layer prior to bulk melting
This surface premelting layer reduces the nucleation barrier for complete melting and propagates inward
The effect is significant only below a critical diameter of ~10–15 nm; above this, bulk thermodynamic properties dominate
DSC and in situ TEM can detect the onset of premelting and the formation of a disordered surface layer
